summary: Pipeline is an ordered stack of StreamTransforms listed outermost-first, matching file-suffix order. apply_read unwraps outer to inner and returns a handle that, on close, closes every distinct layer it built in reverse construction order while leaving the caller's source open; apply_write wraps inner to outer. The same instance serves both directions and is reused by the facade for read, write and cross-backend copy.
key_classes: Pipeline — ordered outermost-first transform stack with is_empty/apply_read/apply_write
_ReadStream — private RawIOBase wrapper that delegates reads/seek/tell and owns an ExitStack of layer closes
key_functions: Pipeline(*transforms: StreamTransform) — construct; order is outermost-first
Pipeline.is_empty() -> bool — whether the pipeline leaves bytes unchanged
Pipeline.apply_read(stream) -> BinaryIO — strip layers outer→inner; returns source unchanged for empty/identity pipelines
Pipeline.apply_write(stream) -> BinaryIO — add layers inner→outer (reverse list order)
extension_points: Accepts any object satisfying the StreamTransform protocol; identity transforms (returning the same stream) are tracked and not double-owned
lifecycle_notes: apply_read ownership: the returned stream owns layers it constructed, not the supplied source; callers close the source separately (docs/read-access-modes.md).
Layer close order is LIFO; layers already closed by a cascading transform are skipped via _close_if_open.
Construction failures unwind built layers and re-raise the original exception; cleanup exceptions during that unwind are swallowed.
apply_write performs no ownership tracking; closing the outermost writer-side reader cascades only as far as each transform's own close() does.
_ReadStream.seek/tell raise io.UnsupportedOperation when the innermost decoded layer is not seekable.
documentation_hooks: Pipeline ordering (outermost-first, suffix order) with a worked gzip-of-gpg example
Stream ownership and close semantics for direct apply_read callers
How the facade chooses direction for read/write/copy_between
examples: examples/gzip_pipeline/example.py — Pipeline/Gzip used via facade write and read
risks: Asymmetric ownership: apply_read never closes the source, but the Gzip write path (GzipCompressingReader) closes its source, so write-side callers get different ownership than read-side.
Cleanup exceptions during a failed apply_read construction are silently discarded (bare except Exception: pass), which can hide resource leaks.
_ReadStream is not thread-safe; read-access-modes docs state handles are not safe for concurrent seek/read.

evidence.detail: apply_read builds ExitStack of _close_if_open callbacks; returns source if len(seen)==1
Documents layer close order and that apply_read does not own the supplied source
